effects.label: B-format pan
effects.blurb: Pan a mono source into 1st-order B-format (4-channel ambisonic W/X/Y/Z), optionally rotating.

effects.label: Resync cycles
effects.blurb: Repeat the source in phasing cyclestreams that drift apart and resynchronise across the output channels (Reich-style phase loops).

effects.label: Crumble to 8 channels
effects.blurb: Project a mono sound onto an 8-channel ring, then progressively crumble it into segments scattered over smaller and smaller channel groups.

effects.label: Crumble to 16 channels
effects.blurb: Like Crumble, but onto a 16-channel ring split down to eight images.

effects.label: Flutter (spatial tremolo)
effects.blurb: Bounce a loudness tremor between the left and right channels, fluttering the sound around the stereo field.

effects.label: Fracture (fragment scatter)
effects.blurb: Shatter the source into enveloped fragments dealt out across the channels in pulsing waves.

effects.label: Spatial syncopation
effects.blurb: Repeat the source as a pulse in spatially separated streams, randomly deleting repeats to syncopate the rhythm around the space.

effects.label: Multichannel spread
effects.blurb: Spread a mono source outward from a centre channel across a multichannel field.

effects.label: Shred to multichannel
effects.blurb: Cut the sound into random chunks and reassemble them in random order, spraying the segments across a multichannel field.

effects.label: Pan (mono → stereo)
effects.blurb: Place a (mono-mixed) source at a position in the stereo field.

effects.label: Spread to channels
effects.blurb: Place each input sound on its own output channel (N mono sounds → an N-channel file). Supply the extra sounds as extra.inputs.

effects.label: Distribute across N channels
effects.blurb: Deal the input sounds, in order, across a fixed number of output channels. Supply the extra sounds as extra.inputs.

effects.label: Spatial panorama
effects.blurb: Distribute several mono sounds around a ring of loudspeakers, spread from left to right. Supply the extra sounds as extra.inputs.

effects.label: Stereo enhance
effects.blurb: Widen a stereo image by phase-cancelling each channel out of the other.

effects.label: Phasing (multi-stream)
effects.blurb: Classic phasing from several phase-shifted copies of a mono source, spread across the output channels.

effects.label: Spin stereo image
effects.blurb: Spin a (stereo) image around the stereo field, with optional doppler.

effects.label: Tangent motion (8ch)
effects.blurb: Play repetitions of a mono sound along a tangent path to or from an 8-channel loudspeaker ring.

effects.label: Tesselate (phase pattern)
effects.blurb: Steve-Reich-style phase pattern: the source repeats across channel pairs whose delays drift apart and resynchronise.

effects.label: Transit motion (8ch)
effects.blurb: Send repetitions of a mono sound crossing an 8-channel loudspeaker ring along a chosen path.

effects.label: Spectral blur
effects.blurb: Time-average the spectrum over N analysis windows.

effects.label: Spectral average
effects.blurb: Average each spectral band with its frequency neighbours.

effects.label: Suppress partials
effects.blurb: Remove the N loudest partials in each window.

effects.label: Spectral chorus
effects.blurb: Chorus by randomising partial amplitudes and frequencies.

effects.label: Drunk walk
effects.blurb: Read the spectrum by a random (drunken) walk over analysis windows.

effects.label: Shuffle windows
effects.blurb: Shuffle the order of spectral analysis windows by a domain→image pattern.

effects.label: Spectral noise
effects.blurb: Inject noise into the spectrum (0 = none, 1 = saturated).

effects.label: Spectral scatter
effects.blurb: Randomly thin the spectrum, keeping N blocks per window.

effects.label: Spread peaks
effects.blurb: Spread the spectral peaks, introducing controlled noisiness.

effects.label: Weave windows
effects.blurb: Read the spectrum by weaving forward and back through the analysis windows.

effects.label: Exaggerate contour
effects.blurb: Exaggerate the spectral contour (sharpen peaks).

effects.label: Fold into range
effects.blurb: Octave-transpose all spectral components into a chosen frequency band.

effects.label: Step-freeze
effects.blurb: Freeze the spectrum at regular time intervals (stepped, stuttering texture).

effects.label: Accumulate
effects.blurb: Sustain each spectral band until louder energy arrives, building an accumulating wash.

effects.label: Focus on peaks
effects.blurb: Concentrate spectral energy onto the strongest peaks (pitch/formant focusing).

effects.label: Hold spectrum
effects.blurb: Freeze the spectrum at a chosen moment and sustain it, stretching the sound.

effects.label: Freeze spectrum
effects.blurb: Freeze the spectral character of the sound from a given moment onward.

effects.label: Glisten (partition)
effects.blurb: Randomly partition the spectrum into sets and play them back in turn.

effects.label: Trace partials
effects.blurb: Retain only the N loudest partials (spectral thinning).

effects.label: Blur + trace
effects.blurb: Time-average the spectrum and then retain only the N loudest partials.

effects.label: Spectral low-pass
effects.blurb: Low-pass the spectrum (frequency-domain).

effects.label: Spectral high-pass
effects.blurb: High-pass the spectrum (frequency-domain).

effects.label: Spectral band-pass
effects.blurb: Band-pass the spectrum between two frequencies (frequency-domain).

effects.label: Spectral notch
effects.blurb: Reject a band of the spectrum between two frequencies (frequency-domain notch).

effects.label: Emphasise changes
effects.blurb: Emphasise moments of spectral change (plucked/transient-like).

effects.label: Arpeggiate spectrum
effects.blurb: Sweep a boosted band up and down the spectrum, arpeggiating its partials.

effects.label: Split-band gain
effects.blurb: Split the spectrum at a frequency and scale the low and high bands independently.

effects.label: Swap FFT real/imag
effects.blurb: Exchange the real and imaginary parts of the sound’s FFT — a metallic, phase-mangled glitch.

effects.label: Invert FFT phase
effects.blurb: Flip the phase of every FFT channel, subtly (or not so subtly) recolouring the sound.

effects.label: Self-similarity
effects.blurb: Replace spectral windows with the louder windows they most resemble, making the sound more self-similar.

effects.label: Narrow formants
effects.blurb: Steepen the formant peaks of the spectrum, sharpening the vowel-like resonances. Needs a pitched source.

effects.label: Invert formants
effects.blurb: Turn formant peaks into troughs and troughs into peaks, optionally cycling between original and inverted.

effects.label: Spectral fold
effects.blurb: Fold a group of spectral channels over on itself, crossing frequency data.

effects.label: Scramble spectral channels
effects.blurb: Randomly permute a group of spectral channels, scattering frequency data.

effects.label: Randomise window order
effects.blurb: Shuffle the time-order of the analysis windows, scrambling the sound’s evolution.

effects.label: Spectral squeeze
effects.blurb: Compress the whole spectrum in frequency around a centre, narrowing its range.

effects.label: Remove a pitch
effects.blurb: Find a pitch in the spectrum and strip it and its harmonics away.

effects.label: Frequency shift
effects.blurb: Slide the whole spectrum by a fixed number of Hz (linear shift → inharmonic/bell-like).

effects.label: Waver (in/harmonic)
effects.blurb: Oscillate between the harmonic sound and a spectrally-stretched inharmonic version.

effects.label: Spectral invert
effects.blurb: Invert the spectrum, turning spectral peaks into troughs (timbral negative).

effects.label: Spectral glissando
effects.blurb: Create an endless Shepard-tone glissando inside the source’s spectral envelope.

effects.label: Spectral stretch
effects.blurb: Stretch the frequencies of the spectrum above the divide point.

effects.label: Super accumulate
effects.blurb: Sustain every spectral band until louder sound arrives there, building a long, ringing resonant wash.

effects.label: Suppress partials
effects.blurb: Remove the N loudest spectral components in a band, leaving the residual noise and halo around them.

effects.label: Bounce
effects.blurb: Bounce the whole sound: accelerating repeats that die away, like a dropped ball settling.

effects.label: Cantor holes (proportional)
effects.blurb: Cantor-set erosion: cut a hole in the middle third, then in the pieces that remain, and so on — output is the growing sequence.

effects.label: Cantor holes (fixed)
effects.blurb: Cantor-set erosion with fixed-length holes: the growing sequence of ever-more-perforated sounds.

effects.label: Cantor vibrato layers
effects.blurb: Cantor-set erosion driven by superimposed vibrato envelopes — a shimmering sequence of perforated sounds.

effects.label: Cascade echoes
effects.blurb: Echo successive segments of the source and superimpose the echo-sets.

effects.label: Tighten silences
effects.blurb: Shorten (or close up) the silent gaps in a sound, tightening its rhythm.

effects.label: Cut to enveloped grains
effects.blurb: Chop a mono sound into a sequence of separate waveset-grains, each with a falling envelope.

effects.label: Segment zigzag
effects.blurb: Zigzag back and forth across the sound with progressively shrinking sweeps.

effects.label: Fast wind
effects.blurb: Shorten the sound by keeping small clips and skipping between them (fast-wind scan).

effects.label: Cut to enveloped slices
effects.blurb: Chop a mono sound into a sequence of separate fixed-length slices, each with a falling envelope.

effects.label: Repeat syllables
effects.blurb: Detect speech-like syllables and repeat each one (stutter). Needs articulated, speech-like input.

effects.label: Shuffle syllables
effects.blurb: Detect speech-like syllables and reorder them at random (repeatable per seed). Needs articulated input.

effects.label: Loop segment
effects.blurb: Loop a segment from the start of the file a number of times.

effects.label: Iterate (fluid)
effects.blurb: Iterate the whole sound in a fluid manner with random pitch/time scatter.

effects.label: Doublets
effects.blurb: Cut the source into segments and repeat each one (stuttering).

effects.label: Zigzag
effects.blurb: Read back and forth (zigzag) inside the first part of the file.

effects.label: Freeze / sustain
effects.blurb: Freeze a segment and re-sound it to fill a longer duration (granular sustain).

effects.label: Drunk walk
effects.blurb: Splice segments read by a drunken walk around a moving point in the source.

effects.label: Back-to-back
effects.blurb: Abut the sound to a reversed copy of itself at the join point (palindrome).

effects.label: Repeat at times
effects.blurb: Replay the whole source at a series of evenly-spaced times (echo/overlay).

effects.label: Fractalise
effects.blurb: Build a self-similar (fractal) expansion of the sound.

effects.label: Isolate loud segments
effects.blurb: Extract the loud events from a mono sound into one file (they keep their original timing), plus a remnant file of the leftovers.

effects.label: Slice into pieces
effects.blurb: Cut a mono sound into equal-length pieces, each written to its own file.

effects.label: FOF iterate (pitch line)
effects.blurb: Re-sound the source as a rapid stream of short packets at a chosen pitch (FOF-style vocal synthesis), with vibrato and random scatter.

effects.label: Iterate on a pitch line
effects.blurb: Re-sound the source repeatedly while its transposition follows a line from a start to an end pitch.

effects.label: Partition (wavesets)
effects.blurb: Deal a mono sound out across several files in waveset-sized blocks (silence fills the gaps).

effects.label: Partition (time blocks)
effects.blurb: Deal a mono sound out across several files in fixed-length time blocks.

effects.label: Rejoin segments
effects.blurb: Remix segment files from Partition / Isolate back into one sound (the inverse operation). Supply the segments as extra.inputs.

effects.label: Bouncing repeat
effects.blurb: Repeat a segment with accelerating, dimming bounces (like a dropped object settling).

effects.label: Respeed events
effects.blurb: Find silence-separated events and change their speed. Needs rhythmic/percussive input.

effects.label: Shifting cycles
effects.blurb: Layer the sound into simultaneous repeating cycles of different lengths, moving a louder “focus” from one to the next.

effects.label: Shrinking repeats
effects.blurb: Repeat the sound with each repeat shorter than the last, closing up as it goes.

effects.label: Splinter into
effects.blurb: A stream of tiny, rising splinters of the sound leads into it at the chosen point.

effects.label: Splinter away
effects.blurb: The sound plays to the chosen point, then shatters into a stream of shrinking splinters.

effects.label: Stutter
effects.blurb: Slice the source into elements and replay randomly cut segments of them in random order, with optional silences (speech-stutter effect).

effects.label: Brownian texture
effects.blurb: Scatter transposed copies of the source into a stream that drifts through pitch and space by brownian motion.

effects.label: Crystal (rotating vertices)
effects.blurb: Rotate a crystal of vertices in 3-D; each vertex fires an event whose stereo position, pitch and brightness trace the rotation.

effects.label: Motor (pulse engine)
effects.blurb: Machine-like texture: a fast inner pulse-stream cut from the source, driven under a slower rising-and-falling outer envelope.

effects.label: Grain texture (spatial)
effects.blurb: Scatter grains read as drunken walks through the source across a multichannel field.

effects.label: Pulse stream
effects.blurb: Chop the source into short enveloped packets and fire them out as a stream of pulses.

effects.label: Pitched pulses
effects.blurb: A stream of pitched packets: brightness comes from the source, the pitch from the MIDI pitch control.

effects.label: Rotor (note-set cycles)
effects.blurb: Spin the source into note-sets that grow and shrink in pitch-range, speed and stereo width as two cycles drift in and out of phase.

effects.label: Texture (event cloud)
effects.blurb: Scatter copies of the source into a cloud of events at random times and pitches.

effects.label: Clip
effects.blurb: Hard-clip the signal at the given level (distortion).

effects.label: Clip half-waves
effects.blurb: Clip each half-waveform at a fraction of its own peak (level-following distortion).

effects.label: Low-pass filter
effects.blurb: Fixed low-pass: frequencies above the stop band are removed.

effects.label: Boost/cut band
effects.blurb: Boost or cut a band of frequencies centred on a frequency.

effects.label: Sweeping band-pass
effects.blurb: Band-pass filter whose focus frequency sweeps up and down a range.

effects.label: Resonant band-pass
effects.blurb: Resonant band-pass: passes a band around the centre frequency, the rest attenuated.

effects.label: Resonant notch
effects.blurb: Resonant notch (band-reject): removes a band around the centre frequency.

effects.label: Resonant low-pass
effects.blurb: Resonant low-pass with an emphasised cutoff (synth-style).

effects.label: Resonant high-pass
effects.blurb: Resonant high-pass with an emphasised cutoff (synth-style).

effects.label: Phaser
effects.blurb: Classic phasing effect (mix of signal with a phase-shifted copy).

effects.label: Iterated filter bank
effects.blurb: Iterate the sound, cumulatively filtering each repeat through a tuned filter bank.

effects.label: Harmonic filter bank
effects.blurb: A bank of resonant filters tuned to a harmonic series over the root frequency.

effects.label: Noise gate
effects.blurb: Replace sound below the threshold with silence.

effects.label: Gate (remove gaps)
effects.blurb: Edit out (delete) the stretches quieter than the threshold, shortening the sound.

effects.label: Shudder
effects.blurb: Shudder a stereo sound with scattered amplitude dips of random depth and width.

effects.label: Spectral mean
effects.blurb: Combine two sounds by taking the mean of their spectra (a hybrid).

effects.label: Spectral cross
effects.blurb: Replace the spectral amplitudes of the first sound with those of the second (cross-synthesis).

effects.label: Spectral sum
effects.blurb: Add the two spectra together.

effects.label: Spectral difference
effects.blurb: Subtract the second spectrum from the first (spectral cancellation).

effects.label: Spectral interleave
effects.blurb: Interleave alternating blocks of analysis frames from the two sounds.

effects.label: Spectral maximum
effects.blurb: Keep, in every channel and frame, the louder of the two spectra.

effects.label: Convolve
effects.blurb: Convolve the first sound with the second (cross-filtering / impulse-response colouring).

effects.label: Spectral denoise
effects.blurb: Remove noise from the first sound using the second as a noise profile (the second input should be a sample of noise or room tone alone).

effects.label: Amplitude transplant
effects.blurb: Impose the channel amplitudes of the second sound onto the channel frequencies of the first.

effects.label: Spectral multiply
effects.blurb: Multiply the two spectra together — only frequencies present in both sounds survive.

effects.label: Subtract signal
effects.blurb: Sample-by-sample subtract the 2nd sound (mixed to mono) from one channel of the 1st — cancel shared material or take a difference.

effects.label: Waveset interpolate (marks)
effects.blurb: Rebuild the sound by interpolating between waveset-groups found at marked times (glassy waveset morphing).

effects.label: Waveset octave-up
effects.blurb: Double (or quadruple…) the frequency of each waveset — octave shifts up.

effects.label: Waveset multiply
effects.blurb: Repeat each waveset N times (raises pitch, adds grit).

effects.label: Waveset average
effects.blurb: Average groups of wavesets together.

effects.label: Waveset reverse
effects.blurb: Reverse wavesets in groups.

effects.label: Waveset interpolate
effects.blurb: Interpolate between successive wavesets (stretches & smears).

effects.label: Waveset telescope
effects.blurb: Telescope (compress) groups of wavesets into one.

effects.label: Waveset divide
effects.blurb: Divide each wavecycle, adding subharmonics.

effects.label: Waveset delete
effects.blurb: Time-contract by keeping only 1 in every N wave-cycles.

effects.label: Waveset replace
effects.blurb: In each group of N wave-cycles, the strongest replaces the rest.

effects.label: Waveset band-filter
effects.blurb: Drop wave-cycles outside a pseudo-frequency band (waveset band-pass).

effects.label: Waveset pitchwarp
effects.blurb: Randomly pitch-warp each wave-cycle (warbly, granular detuning).

effects.label: Waveset omit
effects.blurb: Silence A out of every B wavesets (gappy, rhythmic thinning).

effects.label: Waveset repeat
effects.blurb: Repeat each wavecycle N times without time-stretching (roughens, lowers pitch).

effects.label: Waveset overload
effects.blurb: Clip the signal and overlay a noise distortion pattern on the clipped parts.

effects.label: Waveset reform
effects.blurb: Exaggerate the contour of each wavecycle (sharper, brighter).

effects.label: Waveset fractal
effects.blurb: Superimpose miniature copies of each wavecycle onto itself (fractal graininess).

effects.label: Waveset envelope
effects.blurb: Impose a rising amplitude envelope over each group of N wavecycles (rhythmic pulsing).

effects.label: Harmonic distortion
effects.blurb: Superimpose chosen harmonics onto each wavecycle (adds richness/grit).

effects.label: Waveset elongate
effects.blurb: Repeat each wavecycle N times, stretching the sound in time and lowering its pitch.

effects.label: Waveset group-repeat
effects.blurb: Repeat groups of wavesets until the requested duration is filled.

effects.label: Wavecycle repeat-stretch
effects.blurb: Time-stretch by repeating each wave-cycle group (with splices).

effects.label: Half-cycle shift
effects.blurb: Shift alternate groups of half-wavecycles forward in time.

effects.label: Half-cycle swap
effects.blurb: Swap alternate groups of half-wavecycles.

effects.label: Power distort
effects.blurb: Raise the waveform to a power — below 1 adds grit, above 1 smooths.

effects.label: Waveset scramble
effects.blurb: Randomly reorder wavesets from the source.

effects.label: Tremolo (envelope)
effects.blurb: Impose a tremolo (amplitude) envelope on the sound.

effects.label: Swell
effects.blurb: Fade in to and out from a peak moment (peak must be within the file).

effects.label: Emphasise attack
effects.blurb: Boost the loudest point as an attack transient.

effects.label: Fade in/out (dovetail)
effects.blurb: Dovetail the file by fading the start in and the end out.

effects.label: Fade to silence
effects.blurb: Fade the sound to silence starting at a given time within it.

effects.label: Amplitude ramp
effects.blurb: Impose a linear amplitude ramp across the whole sound (crescendo / decrescendo).

effects.label: Exponential decay
effects.blurb: Impose an exponential fade-to-silence from a chosen start time.

effects.label: Peak chop
effects.blurb: Isolate the attack peaks and replay them at a set tempo. Needs rhythmic input.

effects.label: Level (equalise)
effects.blurb: Even out the loudness of successive sound elements (levels the dynamics).

effects.label: Spike envelope
effects.blurb: Envelope the whole sound to swell to a single peak at a chosen time.

effects.label: Tremolo (narrowing)
effects.blurb: Tremolo whose width narrows after each peak.

effects.label: Tremolo
effects.blurb: Amplitude modulation (tremolo).

effects.label: Convolution reverb
effects.blurb: Convolve the sound with an impulse response (reverb IR or FIR filter) on the 2nd input.

effects.label: Multichannel echoes
effects.blurb: Scatter decaying "stadium" echoes of the source around a multichannel field.

effects.label: Delay / resonance
effects.blurb: Delay with feedback — short times give resonance, long times give echo.

effects.label: Tuned delay
effects.blurb: Short tuned delay producing a resonant pitch.

effects.label: Reverb
effects.blurb: Algorithmic multichannel reverb (fills 1–8 output channels).

effects.label: Room reverb
effects.blurb: Room-model multichannel reverb with small/medium/large presets.

effects.label: Echoes
effects.blurb: Discrete, non-overlapping echoes of the whole sound, dying away.

effects.label: Vocoder (cross-synth)
effects.blurb: Impose the spectral envelope (formants) of the second sound onto the first.

effects.label: Envelope transfer
effects.blurb: Replace the spectral envelope of the first sound with that of the second (the second sound must be at least as long as the first).

effects.label: Spectral twin
effects.blurb: Build a hybrid of the two sounds by exchanging their spectral frequencies and envelopes.

effects.label: Fractal wave
effects.blurb: Recursively transpose the sound over a self-similar pitch pattern — a fractal cascade of speed-ups and slow-downs.

effects.label: Transpose (speed)
effects.blurb: Vary speed and pitch together by a number of semitones.

effects.label: Gain
effects.blurb: Scale the loudness of the sound.

effects.label: Stack (harmoniser)
effects.blurb: Stack transposed copies of the source on the original (octave/chord doubler).

effects.label: Time stretch (smooth)
effects.blurb: Phase-vocoder time-stretch that breaks up channel coherence to suppress the usual stretch artefacts.

effects.label: Accelerando
effects.blurb: Accelerate (or decelerate) smoothly towards a goal speed, tape-style (pitch follows).

effects.label: Vibrato
effects.blurb: Add vibrato: wobble the pitch of the sound at a set rate and depth.

effects.label: Time stretch
effects.blurb: Phase-vocoder time-stretch without changing pitch.

effects.label: Verge glisses
effects.blurb: Play the source with brief pitch-gliss "verges" swooping onto chosen moments.

effects.label: Duplicate grains
effects.blurb: Repeat each detected grain N times. Needs rhythmic/percussive input.

effects.label: Grain time-warp
effects.blurb: Stretch the time between grains without stretching the grains. Needs rhythmic input.

effects.label: Reverse grain order
effects.blurb: Reverse the order of grains without reversing the grains. Needs rhythmic input.

effects.label: Omit grains
effects.blurb: Keep K out of every N detected grains (rhythmic thinning). Needs rhythmic input.

effects.label: Reorder grains
effects.blurb: Reorder grains following a fixed jump pattern. Needs rhythmic input.

effects.label: Align grains (2 sounds)
effects.blurb: Retime the grains of the second sound onto the grain-onset times of the first.

effects.label: Repitch grains
effects.blurb: Transpose each detected grain by a number of semitones. Needs rhythmic input.

effects.label: Extend grain region
effects.blurb: Find grains in a region of the sound and extend it by repeating them. Needs rhythmic/grainy input.

effects.label: Hover (zigzag read)
effects.blurb: Hover over a point in the file, zigzag-reading it at a frequency.

effects.label: Hover 2 (symmetric zigzag)
effects.blurb: Hover over a point in the file, zigzag-reading it into symmetrical zero-centred waveforms.

effects.label: Granular pitch-shift
effects.blurb: Granular reconstitution that pitch-shifts the source (transposition ratio).

effects.label: Wrappage (spatial brassage)
effects.blurb: Granulate the source and scatter the grains over a multichannel field, with time-stretch or freeze and pitch shift.

effects.label: Split channels
effects.blurb: Split a sound into its channels, one mono file each (left first) — a bank of sounds.

effects.label: Mix two sounds
effects.blurb: Mix the first and second sounds together (mono or stereo), with optional offset and balance.

effects.label: Join channels (interleave)
effects.blurb: Interleave two (mono) sounds into one stereo file: first → left, second → right. The inverse of Split channels.

effects.label: Spectral morph
effects.blurb: Interpolate (morph) from the first sound into the second over a span of time.

effects.label: Spectral bridge
effects.blurb: Interpolate across the whole sound between the two spectra (a bridge from one to the other).

effects.label: Peak morph
effects.blurb: Morph between dissimilar spectra by moving the spectral peaks of the first sound onto those of the second.

effects.label: Tune to harmonic field
effects.blurb: Gradually tune the first sound to the (averaged) harmonic field of the second.

effects.label: Partial cross
effects.blurb: Interpolate the partials of one pitched sound towards those of another (both sounds must be clearly pitched).

effects.label: Sound packet
effects.blurb: Isolate/shape one enveloped sound packet (a short grain) from the source.

effects.label: Make wavetable
effects.blurb: Extract a short segment and mirror it into a symmetric wavecycle — a wavetable cut from the sound.

effects.label: Wavetable (half-wavesets)
effects.blurb: Build a wavetable from a group of half-wavesets at a point in the sound.

effects.label: Wavetable + sine
effects.blurb: Make a wavetable by crossing a sound segment with a sine wave.

effects.label: Transpose part of spectrum
effects.blurb: Transpose only the part of the spectrum above a split frequency.

effects.label: Pick harmonics
effects.blurb: Keep only the spectral channels near the harmonics of a fundamental (pitch sieve).

effects.label: Tune to pitch
effects.blurb: Replace the spectral frequencies with harmonics of a target pitch (spectral retuning).

effects.label: Spectral chord
effects.blurb: Superimpose transposed copies of the spectrum on the original, building a chord.

effects.label: Octave up (keep formants)
effects.blurb: Transpose up by an octave (or harmonic ratio) without shifting the formants. Needs a pitched source.

effects.label: Octave down (keep formants)
effects.blurb: Transpose down by an octave (or harmonic ratio) without shifting the formants. Needs a pitched source.

effects.label: Delete alternate harmonics
effects.blurb: Delete the odd harmonics — an octave-up transposition with no formant change (hollow, clarinet-like). Needs a pitched source.

effects.label: Transpose spectrum
effects.blurb: Transpose the spectrum (the spectral envelope moves with it).

effects.label: Transpose (keep formants)
effects.blurb: Transpose the pitch while keeping the formant envelope in place (voice keeps its character).

effects.label: Auto-tune (nearest note)
effects.blurb: Find the most prominent pitch in the sound and transpose it to the nearest tempered (keyboard) note.

effects.label: Tune to chord
effects.blurb: Pull the spectrum onto the harmonics of a chosen chord (spectral retuning to several pitches at once).

effects.label: Pitch-sync stretch
effects.blurb: Time-stretch by repositioning pitch-synchronous grains. Pitch is auto-detected; the hint is used if none is found.

effects.label: Pitch-sync duplicate
effects.blurb: Lengthen by duplicating pitch-synchronous grains. Pitch is auto-detected; the hint is used if none is found.

effects.label: Freeze grain (sustain)
effects.blurb: Freeze and sustain a single grain into a held tone, with optional vibrato.

effects.label: Tweets
effects.blurb: Replace the voiced pulses of the sound with synthetic birdsong-like tweets. Pitch is auto-detected; the hint is used if none is found.

effects.label: Pulses to noise
effects.blurb: Replace the voiced pulses of the sound with bursts of noise (whispered/breathy version of the source).

effects.label: Quantise pitch (autotune)
effects.blurb: Snap the detected pitch to a major scale (autotune), preserving formants. Needs a pitched, monophonic source.

effects.label: Smooth pitch (de-vibrato)
effects.blurb: Smooth the detected pitch contour over a time window (removes vibrato/jitter). Needs a pitched source.

effects.label: Invert pitch contour
effects.blurb: Mirror the detected pitch contour around a pivot pitch (melodic inversion). Needs a pitched source.

generators.label: Waveform
generators.blurb: Simple oscillator: sine, square, triangle or sawtooth. The non-sine shapes are not band-limited, so they alias at high frequencies.

generators.label: Silence
generators.blurb: A silent soundfile of any length — useful for splicing gaps between sounds.

generators.label: Spectral band
generators.blurb: A warbled tone of varying pitch within a spectral band around a centre frequency.

generators.label: Chord
generators.blurb: Chord from a list of MIDI notes (or frequencies) on a sine wave.

generators.label: Click track
generators.blurb: Clicktrack with a click at each listed time — good for triggering grains.

generators.label: Impulse train
generators.blurb: Stream of impulses — good for driving grain effects.

generators.label: Nested oscillator
generators.blurb: An oscillation modulated by a nested oscillation.

generators.label: Spline synth
generators.blurb: Evolving timbres from smoothly-joined random points.

generators.label: Additive synth
generators.blurb: Additive synthesis from a user-defined (harmonic or inharmonic) spectrum of partials.

generators.label: Wave-packet synth
generators.blurb: Streams of enveloped wave-packets built from a user-defined spectrum.

generators.label: Fractal synth
generators.blurb: A buzzy tone made of spikes distributed fractally over the wavelength.

generators.label: Multisynth (score)
generators.blurb: Triggers and mixes a small set of built-in instrument sounds from a score (low-fi).

generators.label: Strands (pitch spiral)
generators.blurb: Spiralling pitch-stream texture: bands of threads cycling around one another in pitch.

README.title: cdp-web
README.html:
⚠ WORK IN PROGRESS — this documentation is a work in progress

cdp-web

A retro computing themed node-graph patcher front-end for the Composers Desktop Project webassembly port (cdp-wasm).

Sounds are built on a modular desktop: each process is a small window you wire to others with patch cables, so you can audition a whole chain and tweak it as you listen.

Note: the process/nodes are based on a curated catalog of cdp programs. These provide a layer of abstraction over the cdp programs. It's possible to use the raw cdp programs too.

How the patcher works

1. Add a process. Use the menus (or double-click the empty desktop to search) to drop a process onto the desktop. There are three families: sound effects, generators that make sound from nothing, and Faust devices you can program yourself. 2. Give it a sound. Drop an audio file from your computer anywhere on the desktop (it becomes a Source window), use a Source's Choose file… / URL… buttons, or start from a generator. Cables carry audio from one node's output ○ to the next node's input ○. 3. Set the controls. Each parameter has a slider and a plain-language description. Right-click a slider to type an exact value. Many parameters can also *change over time* — see Breakpoint envelopes. 4. Render and listen. Render the chain and play the result. Turn on Options ▸ Auto Render to re-render automatically as you make changes.

Finding your way around

  • Recipes — ready-made patches (File ▸ Recipes) that render a sound the moment you open them; the quickest way to hear what CDP can do.
  • Effect reference — every sound-transforming process, grouped by category, with its parameters explained.
  • Generators — synths and noise sources that create audio from scratch.
  • Faust nodes — write your own DSP (or start from a preset) and run it right in the graph.
  • Concepts guide — a few ideas that pay off across many processes: time-varying parameters, spectral (phase-vocoder) effects, and how stereo is handled.
  • Saving & sharing — .cdp patch files, saving to a chosen location, and sharing a whole patch as a link.

The sidebar has two tabs: Manual, which is this prose — overview, guides, recipes, release notes — and Reference (also Help ▸ Reference…), which is every effect and generator.

Two names for one thing: the menus show a process by the name the catalog gives it (*Shudder*), while the reference pages are filed under the CDP program it belongs to (modify). Reference lists them either way — Catalog groups them by the categories the Process and Generate menus use, CDP lists the program pages — and its search box matches both names, so shudder and modify each find the entry.

Every entry carries a + Add to patch button, which drops that process onto the desktop as a window (the manual closes so you can see it land). Going the other way, right-click any node's title bar and choose Manual… to open its entry.

New to CDP? Check the concepts guide, then browse the effect reference and start patching.

Already know CDP? Start with the catalog and CDP — each process here is one *mode* of one CDP program, with its arguments named and ranged for a slider. That page shows what the curation decided, and how to run any bundled program with CDP's own arguments instead.

effects/README.title: Effect reference
effects/README.html:
Effect reference

⚠ WORK IN PROGRESS — this page is being written and checked against CDP’s reference; details may be wrong or incomplete.

232 effects across 110 CDP programs, grouped by category. Each links to its program page.

Each effect is one mode of one CDP program, with named parameters and ranges chosen for musical use. If you already know CDP, read The catalog and CDP first — it explains what that curation decides on your behalf and how to run the raw program instead.

Combine

  • Spectral mean — combine.mean — Combine two sounds by taking the mean of their spectra (a hybrid).
  • Spectral cross — combine.cross — Replace the spectral amplitudes of the first sound with those of the second (cross-synthesis).
  • Spectral sum — combine.sum — Add the two spectra together.
  • Spectral difference — combine.diff — Subtract the second spectrum from the first (spectral cancellation).
  • Spectral interleave — combine.interleave — Interleave alternating blocks of analysis frames from the two sounds.
  • Spectral maximum — combine.max — Keep, in every channel and frame, the louder of the two spectra.
  • Convolve — modify.convolve — Convolve the first sound with the second (cross-filtering / impulse-response colouring).
  • Spectral denoise — speclean.clean — Remove noise from the first sound using the second as a noise profile (the second input should be a sample of noise or room tone alone).
  • Amplitude transplant — specsphinx.impose — Impose the channel amplitudes of the second sound onto the channel frequencies of the first.
  • Spectral multiply — specsphinx.multiply — Multiply the two spectra together — only frequencies present in both sounds survive.
  • Subtract signal — subtract.subtract — Sample-by-sample subtract the 2nd sound (mixed to mono) from one channel of the 1st — cancel shared material or take a difference.

Delay & reverb

  • Convolution reverb — fastconv.reverb — Convolve the sound with an impulse response (reverb IR or FIR filter) on the 2nd input.
  • Multichannel echoes — mchanrev.stadium — Scatter decaying "stadium" echoes of the source around a multichannel field.
  • Delay / resonance — modify.revecho — Delay with feedback — short times give resonance, long times give echo.
  • Tuned delay — newdelay.newdelay — Short tuned delay producing a resonant pitch.
  • Reverb — reverb.reverb — Algorithmic multichannel reverb (fills 1–8 output channels).
  • Room reverb — reverb.room — Room-model multichannel reverb with small/medium/large presets.
  • Echoes — sfecho.echo — Discrete, non-overlapping echoes of the whole sound, dying away.

Envelope

  • Tremolo (envelope) — envel.tremolo — Impose a tremolo (amplitude) envelope on the sound.
  • Swell — envel.swell — Fade in to and out from a peak moment (peak must be within the file).
  • Emphasise attack — envel.attack — Boost the loudest point as an attack transient.
  • Fade in/out (dovetail) — envel.dovetail — Dovetail the file by fading the start in and the end out.
  • Fade to silence — envel.curtail — Fade the sound to silence starting at a given time within it.
  • Amplitude ramp — envel.scaled — Impose a linear amplitude ramp across the whole sound (crescendo / decrescendo).
  • Exponential decay — envnu.expdecay — Impose an exponential fade-to-silence from a chosen start time.
  • Peak chop — envnu.peakchop — Isolate the attack peaks and replay them at a set tempo. Needs rhythmic input.
  • Level (equalise) — flatten.flatten — Even out the loudness of successive sound elements (levels the dynamics).
  • Spike envelope — spike.spike — Envelope the whole sound to swell to a single peak at a chosen time.
  • Tremolo (narrowing) — tremenv.tremenv — Tremolo whose width narrows after each peak.
  • Tremolo — tremolo.tremolo — Amplitude modulation (tremolo).

Extend & segment

  • Bounce — bounce.bounce — Bounce the whole sound: accelerating repeats that die away, like a dropped ball settling.
  • Cantor holes (proportional) — cantor.holes — Cantor-set erosion: cut a hole in the middle third, then in the pieces that remain, and so on — output is the growing sequence.
  • Cantor holes (fixed) — cantor.holesfixed — Cantor-set erosion with fixed-length holes: the growing sequence of ever-more-perforated sounds.
  • Cantor vibrato layers — cantor.vibrato — Cantor-set erosion driven by superimposed vibrato envelopes — a shimmering sequence of perforated sounds.
  • Cascade echoes — cascade.cascade — Echo successive segments of the source and superimpose the echo-sets.
  • Tighten silences — constrict.constrict — Shorten (or close up) the silent gaps in a sound, tightening its rhythm.
  • Cut to enveloped grains — distcut.envelope — Chop a mono sound into a sequence of separate waveset-grains, each with a falling envelope.
  • Segment zigzag — distmore.segszig — Zigzag back and forth across the sound with progressively shrinking sweeps.
  • Fast wind — dvdwind.dvdwind — Shorten the sound by keeping small clips and skipping between them (fast-wind scan).
  • Cut to enveloped slices — envcut.envelope — Chop a mono sound into a sequence of separate fixed-length slices, each with a falling envelope.
  • Repeat syllables — envspeak.repeat — Detect speech-like syllables and repeat each one (stutter). Needs articulated, speech-like input.
  • Shuffle syllables — envspeak.shuffle — Detect speech-like syllables and reorder them at random (repeatable per seed). Needs articulated input.
  • Loop segment — extend.loop — Loop a segment from the start of the file a number of times.
  • Iterate (fluid) — extend.iterate — Iterate the whole sound in a fluid manner with random pitch/time scatter.
  • Doublets — extend.doublets — Cut the source into segments and repeat each one (stuttering).
  • Zigzag — extend.zigzag — Read back and forth (zigzag) inside the first part of the file.
  • Freeze / sustain — extend.freeze — Freeze a segment and re-sound it to fill a longer duration (granular sustain).
  • Drunk walk — extend.drunk — Splice segments read by a drunken walk around a moving point in the source.
  • Back-to-back — extend.baktobak — Abut the sound to a reversed copy of itself at the join point (palindrome).
  • Repeat at times — extend.repetitions — Replay the whole source at a series of evenly-spaced times (echo/overlay).
  • Fractalise — frfractal.fractal — Build a self-similar (fractal) expansion of the sound.
  • Isolate loud segments — isolate.threshold — Extract the loud events from a mono sound into one file (they keep their original timing), plus a remnant file of the leftovers.
  • Slice into pieces — isolate.slices — Cut a mono sound into equal-length pieces, each written to its own file.
  • FOF iterate (pitch line) — iterfof.line — Re-sound the source as a rapid stream of short packets at a chosen pitch (FOF-style vocal synthesis), with vibrato and random scatter.
  • Iterate on a pitch line — iterline.iterline — Re-sound the source repeatedly while its transposition follows a line from a start to an end pitch.
  • Partition (wavesets) — partition.wavesets — Deal a mono sound out across several files in waveset-sized blocks (silence fills the gaps).
  • Partition (time blocks) — partition.blocks — Deal a mono sound out across several files in fixed-length time blocks.
  • Rejoin segments — rejoin.rejoin — Remix segment files from Partition / Isolate back into one sound (the inverse operation). Supply the segments as extra.inputs.
  • Bouncing repeat — repeater.bounce — Repeat a segment with accelerating, dimming bounces (like a dropped object settling).
  • Respeed events — retime.speed — Find silence-separated events and change their speed. Needs rhythmic/percussive input.
  • Shifting cycles — shifter.cycles — Layer the sound into simultaneous repeating cycles of different lengths, moving a louder “focus” from one to the next.
  • Shrinking repeats — shrink.shrink — Repeat the sound with each repeat shorter than the last, closing up as it goes.
  • Splinter into — splinter.into — A stream of tiny, rising splinters of the sound leads into it at the chosen point.
  • Splinter away — splinter.outof — The sound plays to the chosen point, then shatters into a stream of shrinking splinters.
  • Stutter — stutter.stutter — Slice the source into elements and replay randomly cut segments of them in random order, with optional silences (speech-stutter effect).

Filter & dynamics

  • Clip — clip.clip — Hard-clip the signal at the given level (distortion).
  • Clip half-waves — clip.half — Clip each half-waveform at a fraction of its own peak (level-following distortion).
  • Low-pass filter — filter.lohi — Fixed low-pass: frequencies above the stop band are removed.
  • Boost/cut band — filter.fixed — Boost or cut a band of frequencies centred on a frequency.
  • Sweeping band-pass — filter.sweeping — Band-pass filter whose focus frequency sweeps up and down a range.
  • Resonant band-pass — filter.bandpass — Resonant band-pass: passes a band around the centre frequency, the rest attenuated.
  • Resonant notch — filter.notch — Resonant notch (band-reject): removes a band around the centre frequency.
  • Resonant low-pass — filter.resonlo — Resonant low-pass with an emphasised cutoff (synth-style).
  • Resonant high-pass — filter.resonhi — Resonant high-pass with an emphasised cutoff (synth-style).
  • Phaser — filter.phasing — Classic phasing effect (mix of signal with a phase-shifted copy).
  • Iterated filter bank — filter.iterated — Iterate the sound, cumulatively filtering each repeat through a tuned filter bank.
  • Harmonic filter bank — filter.bank — A bank of resonant filters tuned to a harmonic series over the root frequency.
  • Noise gate — gate.gate — Replace sound below the threshold with silence.
  • Gate (remove gaps) — gate.edit — Edit out (delete) the stretches quieter than the threshold, shortening the sound.
  • Shudder — modify.shudder — Shudder a stereo sound with scattered amplitude dips of random depth and width.

Formants

  • Vocoder (cross-synth) — formants.vocode — Impose the spectral envelope (formants) of the second sound onto the first.
  • Envelope transfer — specenv.replace — Replace the spectral envelope of the first sound with that of the second (the second sound must be at least as long as the first).
  • Spectral twin — spectwin.hybrid — Build a hybrid of the two sounds by exchanging their spectral frequencies and envelopes.

Granular

  • Duplicate grains — grain.duplicate — Repeat each detected grain N times. Needs rhythmic/percussive input.
  • Grain time-warp — grain.timewarp — Stretch the time between grains without stretching the grains. Needs rhythmic input.
  • Reverse grain order — grain.reverse — Reverse the order of grains without reversing the grains. Needs rhythmic input.
  • Omit grains — grain.omit — Keep K out of every N detected grains (rhythmic thinning). Needs rhythmic input.
  • Reorder grains — grain.reorder — Reorder grains following a fixed jump pattern. Needs rhythmic input.
  • Align grains (2 sounds) — grain.align — Retime the grains of the second sound onto the grain-onset times of the first.
  • Repitch grains — grain.repitch — Transpose each detected grain by a number of semitones. Needs rhythmic input.
  • Extend grain region — grainex.extend — Find grains in a region of the sound and extend it by repeating them. Needs rhythmic/grainy input.
  • Hover (zigzag read) — hover.hover — Hover over a point in the file, zigzag-reading it at a frequency.
  • Hover 2 (symmetric zigzag) — hover2.hover2 — Hover over a point in the file, zigzag-reading it into symmetrical zero-centred waveforms.
  • Granular pitch-shift — modify.brassage — Granular reconstitution that pitch-shifts the source (transposition ratio).
  • Wrappage (spatial brassage) — wrappage.wrappage — Granulate the source and scatter the grains over a multichannel field, with time-stretch or freeze and pitch shift.

Mix

  • Split channels — housekeep.split — Split a sound into its channels, one mono file each (left first) — a bank of sounds.
  • Mix two sounds — submix.merge — Mix the first and second sounds together (mono or stereo), with optional offset and balance.
  • Join channels (interleave) — submix.interleave — Interleave two (mono) sounds into one stereo file: first → left, second → right. The inverse of Split channels.

Morph

  • Spectral morph — morph.morph — Interpolate (morph) from the first sound into the second over a span of time.
  • Spectral bridge — morph.bridge — Interpolate across the whole sound between the two spectra (a bridge from one to the other).
  • Peak morph — newmorph.morph — Morph between dissimilar spectra by moving the spectral peaks of the first sound onto those of the second.
  • Tune to harmonic field — newmorph.tune — Gradually tune the first sound to the (averaged) harmonic field of the second.
  • Partial cross — specross.partials — Interpolate the partials of one pitched sound towards those of another (both sounds must be clearly pitched).

Pitch & time

  • Fractal wave — fractal.wave — Recursively transpose the sound over a self-similar pitch pattern — a fractal cascade of speed-ups and slow-downs.
  • Transpose (speed) — modify.speed — Vary speed and pitch together by a number of semitones.
  • Gain — modify.loudness — Scale the loudness of the sound.
  • Stack (harmoniser) — modify.stack — Stack transposed copies of the source on the original (octave/chord doubler).
  • Time stretch (smooth) — spectstr.stretch — Phase-vocoder time-stretch that breaks up channel coherence to suppress the usual stretch artefacts.
  • Accelerando — strans.accel — Accelerate (or decelerate) smoothly towards a goal speed, tape-style (pitch follows).
  • Vibrato — strans.vibrato — Add vibrato: wobble the pitch of the sound at a set rate and depth.
  • Time stretch — stretch.time — Phase-vocoder time-stretch without changing pitch.
  • Verge glisses — verges.verges — Play the source with brief pitch-gliss "verges" swooping onto chosen moments.

Pitch-data

  • Quantise pitch (autotune) — repitch.quantise — Snap the detected pitch to a major scale (autotune), preserving formants. Needs a pitched, monophonic source.
  • Smooth pitch (de-vibrato) — repitch.smooth — Smooth the detected pitch contour over a time window (removes vibrato/jitter). Needs a pitched source.
  • Invert pitch contour — repitch.invert — Mirror the detected pitch contour around a pivot pitch (melodic inversion). Needs a pitched source.

Pitch-sync grains

  • Pitch-sync stretch — psow.stretch — Time-stretch by repositioning pitch-synchronous grains. Pitch is auto-detected; the hint is used if none is found.
  • Pitch-sync duplicate — psow.dupl — Lengthen by duplicating pitch-synchronous grains. Pitch is auto-detected; the hint is used if none is found.
  • Freeze grain (sustain) — psow.sustain — Freeze and sustain a single grain into a held tone, with optional vibrato.
  • Tweets — tweet.tweet — Replace the voiced pulses of the sound with synthetic birdsong-like tweets. Pitch is auto-detected; the hint is used if none is found.
  • Pulses to noise — tweet.noise — Replace the voiced pulses of the sound with bursts of noise (whispered/breathy version of the source).

Spatialisation

  • B-format pan — abfpan.bformat — Pan a mono source into 1st-order B-format (4-channel ambisonic W/X/Y/Z), optionally rotating.
  • Resync cycles — ceracu.cycles — Repeat the source in phasing cyclestreams that drift apart and resynchronise across the output channels (Reich-style phase loops).
  • Crumble to 8 channels — crumble.crumble — Project a mono sound onto an 8-channel ring, then progressively crumble it into segments scattered over smaller and smaller channel groups.
  • Crumble to 16 channels — crumble.crumble16 — Like Crumble, but onto a 16-channel ring split down to eight images.
  • Flutter (spatial tremolo) — flutter.flutter — Bounce a loudness tremor between the left and right channels, fluttering the sound around the stereo field.
  • Fracture (fragment scatter) — fracture.fracture — Shatter the source into enveloped fragments dealt out across the channels in pulsing waves.
  • Spatial syncopation — madrid.syncopate — Repeat the source as a pulse in spatially separated streams, randomly deleting repeats to syncopate the rhythm around the space.
  • Multichannel spread — mchanpan.spread — Spread a mono source outward from a centre channel across a multichannel field.
  • Shred to multichannel — mchshred.shred — Cut the sound into random chunks and reassemble them in random order, spraying the segments across a multichannel field.
  • Pan (mono → stereo) — modify.space — Place a (mono-mixed) source at a position in the stereo field.
  • Spread to channels — multimix.spread — Place each input sound on its own output channel (N mono sounds → an N-channel file). Supply the extra sounds as extra.inputs.
  • Distribute across N channels — multimix.channels — Deal the input sounds, in order, across a fixed number of output channels. Supply the extra sounds as extra.inputs.
  • Spatial panorama — panorama.spatial — Distribute several mono sounds around a ring of loudspeakers, spread from left to right. Supply the extra sounds as extra.inputs.
  • Stereo enhance — phase.stereo — Widen a stereo image by phase-cancelling each channel out of the other.
  • Phasing (multi-stream) — phasor.phasor — Classic phasing from several phase-shifted copies of a mono source, spread across the output channels.
  • Spin stereo image — spin.stereo — Spin a (stereo) image around the stereo field, with optional doppler.
  • Tangent motion (8ch) — tangent.tangent — Play repetitions of a mono sound along a tangent path to or from an 8-channel loudspeaker ring.
  • Tesselate (phase pattern) — tesselate.tesselate — Steve-Reich-style phase pattern: the source repeats across channel pairs whose delays drift apart and resynchronise.
  • Transit motion (8ch) — transit.transit — Send repetitions of a mono sound crossing an 8-channel loudspeaker ring along a chosen path.

Spectral

  • Spectral blur — blur.blur — Time-average the spectrum over N analysis windows.
  • Spectral average — blur.avrg — Average each spectral band with its frequency neighbours.
  • Suppress partials — blur.suppress — Remove the N loudest partials in each window.
  • Spectral chorus — blur.chorus — Chorus by randomising partial amplitudes and frequencies.
  • Drunk walk — blur.drunk — Read the spectrum by a random (drunken) walk over analysis windows.
  • Shuffle windows — blur.shuffle — Shuffle the order of spectral analysis windows by a domain→image pattern.
  • Spectral noise — blur.noise — Inject noise into the spectrum (0 = none, 1 = saturated).
  • Spectral scatter — blur.scatter — Randomly thin the spectrum, keeping N blocks per window.
  • Spread peaks — blur.spread — Spread the spectral peaks, introducing controlled noisiness.
  • Weave windows — blur.weave — Read the spectrum by weaving forward and back through the analysis windows.
  • Exaggerate contour — focus.exag — Exaggerate the spectral contour (sharpen peaks).
  • Fold into range — focus.fold — Octave-transpose all spectral components into a chosen frequency band.
  • Step-freeze — focus.step — Freeze the spectrum at regular time intervals (stepped, stuttering texture).
  • Accumulate — focus.accu — Sustain each spectral band until louder energy arrives, building an accumulating wash.
  • Focus on peaks — focus.focus — Concentrate spectral energy onto the strongest peaks (pitch/formant focusing).
  • Hold spectrum — focus.hold — Freeze the spectrum at a chosen moment and sustain it, stretching the sound.
  • Freeze spectrum — focus.freeze — Freeze the spectral character of the sound from a given moment onward.
  • Glisten (partition) — glisten.glisten — Randomly partition the spectrum into sets and play them back in turn.
  • Trace partials — hilite.trace — Retain only the N loudest partials (spectral thinning).
  • Blur + trace — hilite.bltr — Time-average the spectrum and then retain only the N loudest partials.
  • Spectral low-pass — hilite.splow — Low-pass the spectrum (frequency-domain).
  • Spectral high-pass — hilite.sphigh — High-pass the spectrum (frequency-domain).
  • Spectral band-pass — hilite.spband — Band-pass the spectrum between two frequencies (frequency-domain).
  • Spectral notch — hilite.spnotch — Reject a band of the spectrum between two frequencies (frequency-domain notch).
  • Emphasise changes — hilite.pluck — Emphasise moments of spectral change (plucked/transient-like).
  • Arpeggiate spectrum — hilite.arpeg — Sweep a boosted band up and down the spectrum, arpeggiating its partials.
  • Split-band gain — hilite.band — Split the spectrum at a frequency and scale the low and high bands independently.
  • Swap FFT real/imag — matrix.swap — Exchange the real and imaginary parts of the sound’s FFT — a metallic, phase-mangled glitch.
  • Invert FFT phase — matrix.invphase — Flip the phase of every FFT channel, subtly (or not so subtly) recolouring the sound.
  • Self-similarity — selfsim.selfsim — Replace spectral windows with the louder windows they most resemble, making the sound more self-similar.
  • Narrow formants — specfnu.narrow — Steepen the formant peaks of the spectrum, sharpening the vowel-like resonances. Needs a pitched source.
  • Invert formants — specfnu.vibrate — Turn formant peaks into troughs and troughs into peaks, optionally cycling between original and inverted.
  • Spectral fold — specfold.fold — Fold a group of spectral channels over on itself, crossing frequency data.
  • Scramble spectral channels — specfold.randomise — Randomly permute a group of spectral channels, scattering frequency data.
  • Randomise window order — specnu.rand — Shuffle the time-order of the analysis windows, scrambling the sound’s evolution.
  • Spectral squeeze — specnu.squeeze — Compress the whole spectrum in frequency around a centre, narrowing its range.
  • Remove a pitch — specnu.remove — Find a pitch in the spectrum and strip it and its harmonics away.
  • Frequency shift — strange.shift — Slide the whole spectrum by a fixed number of Hz (linear shift → inharmonic/bell-like).
  • Waver (in/harmonic) — strange.waver — Oscillate between the harmonic sound and a spectrally-stretched inharmonic version.
  • Spectral invert — strange.invert — Invert the spectrum, turning spectral peaks into troughs (timbral negative).
  • Spectral glissando — strange.glis — Create an endless Shepard-tone glissando inside the source’s spectral envelope.
  • Spectral stretch — stretch.spectrum — Stretch the frequencies of the spectrum above the divide point.
  • Super accumulate — superaccu.superaccu — Sustain every spectral band until louder sound arrives there, building a long, ringing resonant wash.
  • Suppress partials — suppress.partials — Remove the N loudest spectral components in a band, leaving the residual noise and halo around them.

Spectral pitch

  • Transpose part of spectrum — pitch.transp — Transpose only the part of the spectrum above a split frequency.
  • Pick harmonics — pitch.pick — Keep only the spectral channels near the harmonics of a fundamental (pitch sieve).
  • Tune to pitch — pitch.tune — Replace the spectral frequencies with harmonics of a target pitch (spectral retuning).
  • Spectral chord — pitch.chord — Superimpose transposed copies of the spectrum on the original, building a chord.
  • Octave up (keep formants) — pitch.octmove — Transpose up by an octave (or harmonic ratio) without shifting the formants. Needs a pitched source.
  • Octave down (keep formants) — pitch.octmovedn — Transpose down by an octave (or harmonic ratio) without shifting the formants. Needs a pitched source.
  • Delete alternate harmonics — pitch.altharms — Delete the odd harmonics — an octave-up transposition with no formant change (hollow, clarinet-like). Needs a pitched source.
  • Transpose spectrum — repitch.transpose — Transpose the spectrum (the spectral envelope moves with it).
  • Transpose (keep formants) — specfnu.transpose — Transpose the pitch while keeping the formant envelope in place (voice keeps its character).
  • Auto-tune (nearest note) — spectune.nearest — Find the most prominent pitch in the sound and transpose it to the nearest tempered (keyboard) note.
  • Tune to chord — tunevary.chord — Pull the spectrum onto the harmonics of a chosen chord (spectral retuning to several pitches at once).

Synthesis

  • Sound packet — packet.make — Isolate/shape one enveloped sound packet (a short grain) from the source.
  • Make wavetable — waveform.make — Extract a short segment and mirror it into a symmetric wavecycle — a wavetable cut from the sound.
  • Wavetable (half-wavesets) — waveform.halfwaves — Build a wavetable from a group of half-wavesets at a point in the sound.
  • Wavetable + sine — waveform.sinemix — Make a wavetable by crossing a sound segment with a sine wave.

Texture

  • Brownian texture — brownian.motion — Scatter transposed copies of the source into a stream that drifts through pitch and space by brownian motion.
  • Crystal (rotating vertices) — crystal.rotate — Rotate a crystal of vertices in 3-D; each vertex fires an event whose stereo position, pitch and brightness trace the rotation.
  • Motor (pulse engine) — motor.motor — Machine-like texture: a fast inner pulse-stream cut from the source, driven under a slower rising-and-falling outer envelope.
  • Grain texture (spatial) — newtex.drunk — Scatter grains read as drunken walks through the source across a multichannel field.
  • Pulse stream — pulser.pulses — Chop the source into short enveloped packets and fire them out as a stream of pulses.
  • Pitched pulses — pulser.pitched — A stream of pitched packets: brightness comes from the source, the pitch from the MIDI pitch control.
  • Rotor (note-set cycles) — rotor.rotor — Spin the source into note-sets that grow and shrink in pitch-range, speed and stereo width as two cycles drift in and out of phase.
  • Texture (event cloud) — texture.simple — Scatter copies of the source into a cloud of events at random times and pitches.

Waveset distortion

  • Waveset interpolate (marks) — distmark.interp — Rebuild the sound by interpolating between waveset-groups found at marked times (glassy waveset morphing).
  • Waveset octave-up — distmore.double — Double (or quadruple…) the frequency of each waveset — octave shifts up.
  • Waveset multiply — distort.multiply — Repeat each waveset N times (raises pitch, adds grit).
  • Waveset average — distort.average — Average groups of wavesets together.
  • Waveset reverse — distort.reverse — Reverse wavesets in groups.
  • Waveset interpolate — distort.interpolate — Interpolate between successive wavesets (stretches & smears).
  • Waveset telescope — distort.telescope — Telescope (compress) groups of wavesets into one.
  • Waveset divide — distort.divide — Divide each wavecycle, adding subharmonics.
  • Waveset delete — distort.delete — Time-contract by keeping only 1 in every N wave-cycles.
  • Waveset replace — distort.replace — In each group of N wave-cycles, the strongest replaces the rest.
  • Waveset band-filter — distort.cyclefilter — Drop wave-cycles outside a pseudo-frequency band (waveset band-pass).
  • Waveset pitchwarp — distort.pitch — Randomly pitch-warp each wave-cycle (warbly, granular detuning).
  • Waveset omit — distort.omit — Silence A out of every B wavesets (gappy, rhythmic thinning).
  • Waveset repeat — distort.repeat — Repeat each wavecycle N times without time-stretching (roughens, lowers pitch).
  • Waveset overload — distort.overload — Clip the signal and overlay a noise distortion pattern on the clipped parts.
  • Waveset reform — distort.reform — Exaggerate the contour of each wavecycle (sharper, brighter).
  • Waveset fractal — distort.fractal — Superimpose miniature copies of each wavecycle onto itself (fractal graininess).
  • Waveset envelope — distort.envel — Impose a rising amplitude envelope over each group of N wavecycles (rhythmic pulsing).
  • Harmonic distortion — distort.harmonic — Superimpose chosen harmonics onto each wavecycle (adds richness/grit).
  • Waveset elongate — distort.elongate — Repeat each wavecycle N times, stretching the sound in time and lowering its pitch.
  • Waveset group-repeat — distortt.repeat — Repeat groups of wavesets until the requested duration is filled.
  • Wavecycle repeat-stretch — distrep.stretch — Time-stretch by repeating each wave-cycle group (with splices).
  • Half-cycle shift — distshift.1 — Shift alternate groups of half-wavecycles forward in time.
  • Half-cycle swap — distshift.swap — Swap alternate groups of half-wavecycles.
  • Power distort — quirk.power — Raise the waveform to a power — below 1 adds grit, above 1 smooths.
  • Waveset scramble — scramble.scramble — Randomly reorder wavesets from the source.

See also the generator reference and the conceptual guide.
